answers: Zigbee2MQTT public documentation, read on 2026-10-26 (no interview with the maintainers)

claims.text: Intended purpose: A bridge between Zigbee devices and MQTT. It lets users control their Zigbee devices without the vendor's bridge or gateway and integrate them with whatever smart home software they use.

items.title: Versions of software affecting compliance with the essential cybersecurity requirements

claims.text: Version assessed: zigbee2mqtt 2.14.2, commit 5c0c1c60078e.

items.title: Hardware: photographs or illustrations showing external features, marking and internal layout

claims.text: Hardware illustrations: Software only. It runs on a host system such as a Raspberry Pi or an Intel NUC, with a Zigbee adapter connected over USB, GPIO, or remotely over Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

User information and instructions: Security guidance for users is published as "Securing the installation": run under a dedicated unprivileged user, restrict access to the data directory and to configuration.yaml (chmod 600), keep credentials in a separate secrets file, do not expose the MQTT broker publicly, keep the host and Zigbee2MQTT updated. The page gives no end-of-support date and no vulnerability reporting contact.

items.title: Design and development, including the system architecture

claims.text: System architecture: Three modules. zigbee-herdsman talks to the Zigbee adapter and offers an API to the layers above; zigbee-herdsman-converters maps each device model to the Zigbee clusters it supports; Zigbee2MQTT drives zigbee-herdsman, maps Zigbee messages to MQTT messages and keeps the system state in database.db, a JSON text file of connected devices. Web front ends (zigbee2mqtt-frontend, zigbee2mqtt-windfront) give monitoring and configuration.

items.title: Vulnerability handling: SBOM, coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy, reporting contact, secure distribution of updates

claims.text: Software bill of materials: CycloneDX JSON, 278 components (251 npm, 27 github), generated by syft 1.55.0 on 2026-10-26.
111 of the 278 SBOM components are runtime dependencies according to pnpm-lock.yaml; the rest are development and build tools that do not ship with the product.
Known vulnerabilities at scan time: 18 matches (4 high, 11 medium, 3 low), 18 distinct identifiers, found by grype 0.121.0 with the vulnerability database built 2026-10-25.
10 of the 18 matches are in runtime dependencies (fast-uri 3.1.6, ip-address 10.7.0); the others are in development and build tools.
18 of the 18 matches have a fixed version available upstream.

0 of the 18 CVE identifiers are in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue (version 2026.10.23). The catalogue is a public signal of exploitation, not the Article 14 test, which starts when the manufacturer becomes aware.
Automated dependency updates are configured in the repository: .github/dependabot.yml.
No security policy file in the repository (looked for SECURITY.md, .github/SECURITY.md and docs/SECURITY.md).
Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy: None published. The repository's security page says "No security policy detected".
Vulnerability reporting contact: Reports can be sent privately with the "Report a vulnerability" button on the repository's security page.
Secure distribution of updates: Manual. On Linux the user runs ./update.sh from the Zigbee2MQTT directory. The page describes no signature check and no separate channel for security updates.
